lead: Every number below is the actual value the engine used for that year — pick a year to see it worked through step by step, from the spending target down to the ending balance.
noDetail: No calculation detail for this year (accumulation years only grow and contribute).
noRow: No projection row for this person in the selected calendar year — they're not yet at their starting age then (the projection runs to max age, so post-depletion years still appear, with any unfunded gap shown as a shortfall).
spendingTargetNote: Desired spending inflated to this year, scaled by any spending-phase band, plus one-time outflow events.
benefitsNote: CPP (age-65 amount × the start-age multiplier), OAS (deferral + residency), and any DB/bridge pension.
rrifMinNote: Forced out first once the RRIF exists; taxed as income. Any after-tax excess over the need is redeposited into taxable.
gisNote: Tax-free; reduced 50¢ per dollar of income excluding OAS{{couple}}.
withdrawalsNote: Drawn in your configured order ({{order}}); registered draws are grossed up so the after-tax amount covers the need.
taxableGrossed: Taxable (grossed up on the gain fraction)
cashCushionNote: After-tax reserve, used as a last resort.
rmTopUpNote: Tax-free borrowing against home equity, the true last resort; grows the loan.
transfersNote: Deliberate account→account moves (e.g. an RRSP meltdown into the TFSA). A registered source is a taxable withdrawal: only the after-tax remainder is redeposited. TFSA/taxable/cash sources are after-tax money (no tax).
depositsNote: One-time inflow events landing in the accounts.
shortfallNote: The portfolio is depleted — benefits cover only part of this year's spending target, so this much of the goal goes unmet. The gap shrinks as later benefits (pension, CPP, OAS, GIS) begin.
shortfallEq: spending target {{amount}} − funded by benefits & portfolio
shortfallWarn: this year's plan is underfunded — the money ran out before the spending goal was met.
incomeTaxNote: Tax on total income, minus the tax already counted on benefits, plus the OAS recovery tax.
totalNetIncome: total net income (benefits + employment + registered + gains×inclusion)
taxOnBenefits: tax already counted on benefits alone
splitOut: pension income split OUT to spouse (lowers your tax)
splitIn: pension income split IN from spouse (taxed to you)
taxOnWithdrawals: income tax on this year's withdrawals
totalTaxAll: total tax on ALL income (what a return would show)
taxFoot: Income tax above is only the incremental tax on withdrawals; Total tax adds the tax on the benefits themselves. Both run every year — neither stops at any age while income is received.
splitFootOut: includes the effect of pension-income splitting — tax here can be non-zero even with no withdrawals, because income was transferred to your spouse.
splitFootIn: includes the effect of pension-income splitting — tax here can be non-zero even with no withdrawals, because income was transferred to you.
growthNote: Market growth applied after withdrawals; balances roll into next year.
